content:
The current best estimate for the age of the universe is **13.8 billion years**, with an uncertainty of about ±0.02 billion years.

This figure comes primarily from observations of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation by the Planck satellite mission, combined with our understanding of cosmology and the expansion rate of the universe (the Hubble constant). 

The age is calculated based on:
- Measurements of the CMB, which is the afterglow of the Big Bang
- Observations of distant galaxies and supernovae
- Models of how the universe has expanded over time
- The current composition of matter, dark matter, and dark energy

This 13.8 billion year figure represents the time that has elapsed since the Big Bang, when the universe began expanding from an extremely hot, dense initial state.
